judged_text: deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so find always misses and calendarId is undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined; Google returns 4xx and the event is never removed from the host's calendar even though the booking is cancelled.

record.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so find always misses and calendarId is undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined; Google returns 4xx and the event is never removed from the host's calendar even though the booking is cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` and similarly in `updateEvent`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the case the fallback branch is meant to handle), the `.find()` compares against `externalCalendarId` (undefined/null), so it will not find a match and returns `undefined`. The previous logic used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` as the fallback; this change removes that valid fallback and can yield an undefined `calendarId`, breaking deletes/updates for bookings/references without `externalCalendarId`.
